intro.lede: You said the round-8 pages looked good but felt AI-made, and asked us to fix it all. Here is what caused it, every page reworked, the page change you asked for, pictures, the new project pages, three ways to run an engagement, and the footer. A few things need your decision before anything goes live.

asks.quote: Could you audit and point out what might be causing this page to feel AI?
asks.answer: Eight causes, each shown on a round-8 page beside its round-9 rework.
Every cause is fixed on every page: first in the parts all pages share, then page by page.

asks.quote: Make our website feel a bit more alive and a bit less text-heavy.
asks.answer: Ten of the 18 pages now open on one large thing under the headline: the page's own document, a drawing to scale, or a picture. Headlines write themselves in.

asks.quote: That flickering logo appears for a short while before switching to the next page.
asks.answer: The turn: a graphite panel crosses the screen, the Kelwin mark flickers on, and the next page appears. Every mockup here has it.

asks.quote: There should also be a picture area where there are pictures of the team.
asks.answer: About now has one: your portrait and one working session, labelled until they are shot. Pictures need a change to standing rule 6, written out for your yes.

asks.quote: We can also have dedicated pages for individual short-term project services.
asks.answer: Six fixed-scope projects proposed and one held. The projects page and the first project page are built as mockups.
Three ways to run an engagement, one recommended. About shows the recommended one as a draft.

asks.quote: What if we pull it above it? It feels off being below that line.
asks.answer: Done: the footer logo now sits on the legal line, which hides its lower fifth. One alternative puts it fully above.

status: Mockups, like round 8. Nothing here is live.

Built this round in the live site's code, on the development branch, not published: the menu, with The Lab under The Firm and the copy you approved; the menu's audit door in ink on paper (your C3 note); the corrected read times and the “Inside this layer” links on the homepage; the footer change.
Each page was rebuilt, read again twice against your notes and the eight causes, and fixed. Then checked on desktop, tablet and phone.
The Lab is rebuilt in the new design. Its application is now “Ask for an invitation”, the quiet link beside the red audit button, as on the other pages.

causes.lede: The homepage was composed section by section over seven rounds. The other pages were filled in from one shared rulebook, so the same small devices repeated on all sixteen and added up to a template. These are the eight causes, in plain words. Each one shows a round-8 crop beside the same kind of thing in round 9. Click a picture to see it full size.

items.title: Tiny grey code-font capitals carried words.
items.plain: On the homepage the typewriter-style font mostly carries numbers. On the other pages it carried field names, column heads and status words: up to 21 on one Reports screen, and Contact's field names at 12px.
items.fix: Labels are ordinary words in the site's own face, sentence case, 14px and up. The code font is kept for numbers and dates.
items.caption: Contact's form. Each field had a small grey code-font name and a second label under it. Now each field has one name in plain words, at reading size, and "All fields required" is said once.
items.before_alt: Round 8 Contact form: field names TO, FROM, COMPANY and REPLY TO in small grey monospaced capitals, each with a second label marked required
items.after_alt: Round 9 Contact form: Your name and Work email in plain words above underlined fields, under one line that says all fields are required

items.title: Made-up reference codes.
items.plain: FN·01, R·01–03, Q. 01–06, 01.1 to 03.4, “The Firm / 03”. Nobody used them to find anything. They were the same device as the figure numbers you removed in round 5.
items.fix: Gone. Numbers stay only where order is the content: the method's phases, the readout's parts, legal clauses, the audit's days.
items.caption: The Insights list. The FN codes, the red Read first tag and the code-font dates are gone. Each note is now a title, one line on what it says, and its layer, month and reading time. The first note is read first because it comes first and is set largest.
items.before_alt: Round 8 Insights list: codes FN·01 to FN·03, quoted symptoms, a red READ FIRST tag and dates in grey monospaced capitals
items.after_alt: Round 9 Insights list: Revenue entropy set large with one line under it, then two smaller notes, each with a plain line giving layer, month and reading time

items.title: Every page opened the same way.
items.plain: A label with a numbered breadcrumb, a headline, a red rule, a lede, a three-row facts box, then a thin framed drawing. Sixteen pages, one recipe.
items.fix: Each headline is set for its page, in size, accent and layout. Under it comes the page's own thing: a document, a drawing with a real measure, a picture, or the content itself.
items.caption: Nine page openings, the same nine pages in both. Round 8 is one layout nine times, each with a facts box and a thin drawing. In round 9 the headlines differ, and under each one is that page's own thing: a document, the 13-week drawing, a frame for footage or photographs to come, or the list or form itself.
items.before_alt: Nine round-8 page openings sharing one layout: label row, headline, red rule, lede, three-row facts box and a thin framed drawing
items.after_alt: Nine round-9 page openings with different headline settings and a document, drawing, photo frame, list or form beneath each

items.title: Drawings illustrated ideas instead of showing things.
items.plain: Noise running through a funnel, a knot untangling, a ring: all 1px lines with labels placed by arithmetic. The homepage draws real objects with one solid mass.
items.fix: A drawing stays only where it explains a real thing. It is drawn with weight and carries at most three labels.
items.caption: GTM Intelligence's opening drawing. The ring marked "One quarter" with four coded labels is now the quarter itself: 13 weeks across, a solid bar for each weekly review, a box for each win/loss call, and the readout week in red. Three labels.
items.before_alt: Round 8 GTM Intelligence drawing: a thin ring marked ONE QUARTER on a tick line, with four boxed codes 03.1 to 03.4
items.after_alt: Round 9 GTM Intelligence drawing: thirteen weeks across, solid weekly bars, open win/loss boxes and a red block for the readout in week 13

items.title: Documents looked like app windows.
items.plain: A title bar, a caption describing itself, a footer chip and grey placeholder lines where text should be. The readout alone was drawn seven different ways.
items.fix: Documents are set as real pages: margins, a running head, page numbers, real paragraphs, and the word Specimen said once.
items.caption: The Orchestration Rules on GTM Infrastructure. The app-style window, with its title bar, route diagram, "choose a rule" hint and Specimen tag in the footer, is now a page: a running head with Specimen said once, a title, numbered sections, and each rule written out as When and Then.
items.before_alt: Round 8 Orchestration Rules drawn as an app window: title bar, column heads in code-font capitals, a route diagram and a SPECIMEN tag in the footer
items.after_alt: Round 9 Orchestration Rules set as a paper page: running head marked Specimen, title, numbered sections, and rules in When and Then columns

items.title: After the first screen, everything was the same size.
items.plain: 42px headings over even, small annotation, section after section, with nothing that dominated.
items.fix: Each section has one large thing, a statement, a number, a picture or a document, and everything else steps well down.
items.caption: The Lab's "why" section. A medium heading over paragraphs of even size is now one large statement with one short line under it.
items.before_alt: Round 8 Lab section: a medium heading, then three paragraphs and a closing statement at similar sizes
items.after_alt: Round 9 Lab section: one large statement over two lines and one short line beneath it

items.title: The writing said things twice.
items.plain: The headline, the lede and the facts box repeated each other. Section heads shared one clipped slogan rhythm, sibling pages shared sentence templates, and pages described themselves.
items.fix: Each thing is said once. Section heads are claims a buyer could disagree with, and every page was cut to a word budget.
items.caption: The opening of Who We Work With. Before, the lede restated the headline and a facts box restated both. Now the headline says it once, one line beside it says who it is for, and one link leads to who we turn away.
items.before_alt: Round 8 Who We Work With opening: a headline, a lede that restates it, and a three-row facts box
items.after_alt: Round 9 Who We Work With opening: a headline, one line beside it with a link, and a stand-in picture below

items.title: No human texture.
items.plain: No picture and no voice on any first screen beyond the homepage.
items.fix: Where a picture fits, the page opens on one: footage, a photograph or the page's real document. Until real footage and photographs exist, those places are marked as such. About has a picture area for the founder and a working session.
items.caption: About's first screen. The thin rules drawing is gone. Two frames hold the places for a photograph of the founder at his desk and one of a working session, marked "Photographs to come" until real ones are taken.
items.before_alt: Round 8 About first screen: headline, facts box and a thin rules drawing, no picture
items.after_alt: Round 9 About first screen: headline, one line, and two marked frames for photographs to come

motion.lede: You asked for an animation between pages, like the Palantir recording where the logo flickers before the next page appears. These are real-time recordings of the mockups at desktop width, with no sound. The recorder catches fewer frames than a screen shows, so the quickest moments, the panel moving in and out, look a little stepped here. Open a mockup to see them smooth.

films.title: The turn
films.caption: On GTM Intelligence, a click on Audit request. A graphite panel with a slanted edge slides across, the Kelwin mark flickers on piece by piece, and the panel lifts off the System Audit page. About 1.2 seconds from the click to the new page. Then its headline writes itself in, in under a second.

films.title: Arriving on a page
films.caption: Projects, opened fresh, as from a search result or a typed address. The mark flickers on a graphite screen and the panel lifts. The headline writes itself in, one line after the other, then the sample scope page under it rises as a narrower rectangle and widens to full width. About three seconds from a blank screen to the settled page.

films.title: The alternative: the sheet slide
films.caption: GoNimbly's way, on the same click, for comparison. The System Audit page slides in from the right over GTM Intelligence, which darkens and drifts left beneath it. No mark, and the headline doesn't write itself in: the new page arrives already set. Just under a second.

motion.live_line: Every mockup in this review already has the turn. Open one and follow its links to feel it at full speed.
motion.reduced: Anyone whose device asks for less motion gets none of it. The page is simply there.
motion.footer_line: One small change to the approved footer motion: its last part, the line drawing across and the Kelwin logo rising, now waits until you reach it, so it is seen on phones too.

pictures.lede: You asked for pictures of the team on About, and liked how GoNimbly puts a moving picture under each headline. Standing rule 6 forbids pictures today, so the mockups show them as a proposal, on three pages: About, Narrative Systems and Who We Work With. Nothing goes into the site's rules without your yes.
pictures.rule_now:
No static pictures in the v5 system.
· Build with type, grid, flat colour, rules, numbers, inline-SVG drawings and motion.
· The one exception is the hero film (see Homepage).
pictures.amendment:
Pictures only where they are real.
· Build with type, grid, flat colour, rules, numbers, inline-SVG drawings and motion.
· An interior page may open on a plate of frosted or graded footage or stills, full width, directly under its headline, with a different shot on each page. The plate's frost and grade count as the film's treatment under rule 5.
· About may show real photographs of the team, and of real working sessions, taken with the client's written consent.
· Never stock photographs of people presented as the team, and never AI-generated photographs.
· Until real footage or photographs exist, a plate is labelled: a card naming the shot (“Footage to come”, “Photographs to come”), or a frosted crop of the homepage film tagged “Stand-in”. The v4 photographs never return.
· The hero film stays the homepage's exception (see Homepage).
pictures.brief_lede: Where a page asks for a picture, it shows a card that names the shot and says how to film it, so the cards are also your shoot list. Two shots moved off their pages and wait here: Careers and The Lab now open without a picture.

shots.now: On the page as a card, labelled “Photographs to come”

shots.now: On the page as a card, labelled “Footage to come”

shots.how: A buyer-side working session: two or three people at a table, shot over a shoulder, faces out of focus, a whiteboard or a printed page between them. Frosted and graded like the homepage film.
shots.now: Until it is shot, the page shows a frosted crop of the homepage film, tagged “Stand-in”. It reads mostly as a blurred shoulder. If you prefer, a card with this brief replaces it.

shots.now: Not on the page. Careers opens straight onto its seats, with no picture.

shots.now: Not on the page. The Lab opens on the cover of the Revenue Entropy Index instead.

projects.offer_line: One piece of the system, built on its own, to the same spec as the full install.
projects.lede: You asked for pages for short, single-piece services, so a buyer who needs one thing isn't turned away. Six are proposed and one is held. Two pages are built as mockups: Projects and Email deliverability. The other five are written and get built once you say yes. The full system stays first, and the audit stays the main door.

items.name: Positioning and messaging
items.line: For a company five people describe five ways, with a raise, a launch or the first sales hire close.
items.keeps: The Narrative OS: positioning, message matrix and proof map.

items.name: Email deliverability
items.line: For a company that sends all its email from one domain, whose replies have fallen while the message stayed the same.
items.keeps: A runbook, and sending domains set up to match it.

items.name: ICP and signal map
items.line: For reps who pick accounts by habit, where the ICP is a slide nobody opens.
items.keeps: An ICP from closed-won deals, and a pipeline that refreshes your CRM's accounts.

items.name: CRM blueprint
items.line: For a company where the board's number and the CRM's number disagree.
items.keeps: A written blueprint for one instance, with dedupe and decay automated.

items.name: Win/loss interviews
items.line: For companies losing deals they expected to win, where the CRM says price. It needs buyers willing to talk.
items.keeps: One round of buyer interviews, and the guide for the next round.

items.name: The operating model
items.line: For a company with the audit's readout in hand and a team that can build. It starts after the readout.
items.keeps: The written plan an install would build from.

items.name: Sales narrative
items.line: Held because it needs delivery capacity. It joins the projects page once you confirm the capacity, or once the Narrative Architect seat is filled.
items.keeps: The sales story in one document the reps use: talk tracks, the demo narrative, and answers to the objections that keep coming back.

only_with_system: The quarterly calibration, with its Rebuild Sequence
projects.only_with_system_line: Some parts only work with the whole system running. The projects page names these four, and says a single project ends at handover, with no retainer.

Then either the build, to handover, or a stop, with the reason in writing

lifecycle.lede: In round 8 you asked for ways to structure the whole lifecycle of an engagement. Here are three, one recommended. All three keep your sequence: the first call, the ten-day audit, the readout call, then the proposal.
lifecycle.spine_title: Your sequence, the spine of every system engagement
spine: Call 3, the proposal: scope, price, contract
Your operator, or us on retainer

options.name: The single path
options.summary: Every engagement starts with the System Audit, large or small. A smaller piece is offered only after the readout, as one of three shapes: the full system, one layer first, or the plan only.
good: Your sequence, unchanged, and every approved line stays true.
cost: A buyer who wants one piece faces three calls and ten working days first, and is likely to leave.
Every lead takes audit time while you are solo.

options.name: Two ways in, one spine
options.sub: The system path, plus a short path for projects.
options.summary: The system path is the single path, unchanged. Beside it runs a short path for fixed-scope projects, with a diagnosis built into the first week instead of the audit. Project requests come through Contact, so red still means only the audit. A project can lead into the audit, and then the retainer.
good: Small buyers can ask for one project and aren't turned away. The full system stays preferred.
Each project fits one contractor seat with you reviewing, so you can grow one seat at a time.
cost: “Engagement” has to mean the full system only, so About's first rule and the menu's “Where every engagement begins” stay true as written (one question below asks you to confirm).
A second sales motion while you are solo: a written scope for every project.

options.name: The staged ladder
options.sub: Each phase is its own contract.
options.summary: The method's phases become rungs, each bought separately and each leaving the client something to own. The audit is paid and credited against the next rung.
good: The smallest yes at every step.
A paid audit protects your time.
cost: It changes your sequence: the paid moment moves from the proposal to the audit.
Three to five contracts per client, and a slower path to the full system.

lifecycle.recommended_line: Two ways in, one spine answers your wish not to turn small buyers away without adding a third door. Two things borrowed from the ladder: the retainer is priced by the quarter and renewed at the calibration readout, and you can start charging for the audit later if it books out. One named lead stays with each client from the first call to handover.
lifecycle.cadence_title: The cadence, as drafted on About

rows: A working session with whoever will run the system, and a written note.

cadence.when: After the handover. Your operator runs these; on retainer, we do.
rows: The operating review, ending on what to stop.
The calibration readout and the next Rebuild Sequence.
The audit's four parts, re-read a year on.

That picture is a placeholder for footage, and doubles as its shoot brief: “A seller’s line, rewritten in the buyer’s words.” It is labelled “Footage to come”, with no fake footage.

“What we install” became “Where the pitch comes from”. It opens on “Your messaging is decided on sales calls, by whoever is talking.”, then one plain paragraph names the four documents of your Narrative OS. The coded list of services (01.1 to 01.4, each with a “Ships” key) is gone.

“How it runs” is two plain statements, “We write it once, with your leadership in the room.” and “Then the person who runs it keeps it current.”, with the week, month and quarter beside them. It is marked “Draft, to be confirmed”.
The page ends on its own line, “We line up every version of your pitch and mark the gaps.”, with the red audit button and one onward link, to the 17% window note. The strip of sibling pages is gone.

questions.default: Yes, as Privacy says, once a lawyer has read it. The Lab page stays silent.
options: No client data feeds the Lab
Not decided: take it out of Privacy

questions.title: Who We Work With: the film stand-in, or a shot card
questions.context: It is the only page that opens on a crop of the homepage film, tagged “Stand-in”, and the crop reads mostly as a blurred shoulder; this only matters if you approve the change to rule 6.
questions.default: Keep the stand-in until real footage exists.
options: A shot card: “A deal, explained by someone other than the founder”

questions.title: The shoot list
questions.context: The Pictures section above lists every shot the pages ask for, from Narrative Systems' rewritten line to About's working session, which needs a client's written consent.
questions.default: Shoot them as briefed, once rule 6 changes.

questions.title: Team pictures on About, as people join
questions.context: About shows your portrait and one working session, with no team slots while you are on your own.
questions.default: Add one portrait per person as they join, shot the same way as yours.
options: Keep it to you and the working session

questions.title: “The founding team” while you're on your own
questions.context: The approved homepage offers “a 30-minute call with the founding team” and the audit FAQ says “Ask the founding team”, while About, Contact and Careers name you or “the founder”.
questions.default: Keep the approved wording, since the team is forming, and keep “Talk to the team” as the name of the second door.
options: Say “the founder” where it means you

questions.title: Three promises someone has to keep
questions.context: About says “Rameez reads every audit request”, Careers says “When a seat opens, this list is read first”, and Reports says “We'll email the first one, when a client clears it, to anyone who asks”, with requests kept in the mailbox and no list.
questions.default: Stand behind all three. About's line changes when a Client Partner joins.

questions.title: The invented company in the specimens
questions.context: The readout, the Orchestration Rules and the Rebuild Sequence are all written for one invented company, founder-led and selling forecasting software, say so on the page, and name real tools in its stack such as Salesforce, Outreach and LinkedIn.
questions.default: Keep the invented company and the real tool names.
options: Make the tools generic (the CRM, the sequencing tool)
Follow one of my real audits, anonymized

questions.title: The labels on what isn't confirmed yet
questions.context: Unconfirmed items carry one of three labels: “To be confirmed” for a missing fact, “Draft, to be confirmed” for how we work, and “Proposed, to be confirmed” for the project offer.
questions.default: Keep these three, and take each one off as you confirm its item in this review.

questions.title: No red button on Contact, Careers, Privacy and Terms
questions.context: These four pages end on a quiet link instead of the red “Request a System Audit”: Contact and Careers are the other door, and the legal pages had none when you approved them in round 8.
questions.default: Keep all four quiet.
options: Give all four the red button

questions.title: The homepage's “The fourth is the operating retainer”
questions.context: The approved homepage calls the method's fourth phase the operating retainer, while everywhere else the system is run by your operator or by us on retainer.
questions.default: Keep it as approved.
options: Soften it: “run by your operator or with us on retainer”

questions.title: Three approved headlines that leave one word alone on small phones
questions.context: On a phone, three of your approved headlines end with a word on a line of its own: the note title “Deliverability is / infrastructure.” on every phone; the Audit’s “The real / constraint, / named in writing.” on phones narrower than about 390px, which includes the common 375px iPhones; and Narrative Systems’ “Decide what / the market / hears.” on phones narrower than about 350px. Each is already set as small as a headline can go there; only shorter words would fix it.
questions.default: Keep your approved words, and accept the lone word on those phones.
options: Shorten them for phones (we’ll propose words)

footer.lede: During this round you asked to move the Kelwin logo at the end of the footer above the legal line. It is done, in a way that keeps your round-4 pick. One alternative is shown beside it.
footer.quote: And also, one more thing I feel I noticed that feels kind of off is that Kelwin logo at the end of the footer. Right now, it seems to be present below the privacy and terms line and the audit request line. What if we pull it above it? It feels off being below that line. What if we fix that thing as well while you are at it?
footer.r8_caption: Round 8: the logo below the legal line, cut off by the page's edge

options.name: On the line
options.text: The logo sits on the legal line, which hides its lower fifth. That keeps your round-4 pick: one quiet tone, about 70% of the width, set right, a fifth buried. The legal line is now the page's last edge.

options.name: Above the line
options.text: The whole logo sits above the line, with nothing hidden. It reads tidier, but drops the buried fifth you picked in round 4, and the footer grows taller.

footer.where: A is on every mockup here, and in the live site's code on the development branch. Nothing is live. B exists only as these pictures.
